prior_attempt.rejection: The first correction separated state borders from arrows, but treated stateArrowColor as unconditionally more specific than ArrowColor. Java normalizes both spellings to the same arrowColor style property, so their declarations override in source order.

second_rejection.rejection: The renderer's unified reverse alias lookup was correct for distinct parsed keys, but parse::collapse_reassigned_skinparams had already collapsed repeated raw spellings independently. It retained each raw key's first position, so a later repeated stateArrowColor could still sort before an intervening ArrowColor even though Java canonicalizes all family-arrow aliases before updating one map entry.

failed_broad_validation.implementation: Canonicalize every non-internal parsed skinparam before reassignment collapse.
failed_broad_validation.evidence: The full no-oracle census fell from 11049/11251 to 11033/11251, entirely in preprocessing (264/307 to 248/307), while state remained 882/901. Theme-expanded diagrams exposed the missing provenance boundary.
failed_broad_validation.finding: RustUML appends `__theme` followed by flattened entries from every theme family sub-block. Keys such as classArrowColor, stateArrowColor, and usecaseArrowColor in that synthetic tail represent distinct style scopes selected later by each renderer; they are not one sequence of user SkinParam.setParam calls. Applying Java ordinary-key canonicalization to the synthetic tail merged those scopes and destroyed the family-specific compatibility model.

invariant: Java resolves state-image borders and state-diagram arrows from sibling style signatures. FromSkinparamToStyle maps stateBorderColor to root.element.stateDiagram.state LineColor. Before either its parameter map or style conversion sees an ordinary declaration, SkinParam.cleanForKeySlow lowercases and trims the key, removes underscores and dots, rewrites sequenceParticipant/sequenceActor aliases, rewrites every activity/class/component/object/sequence/state/usecase Arrow prefix to the shared arrow prefix, and rewrites a terminal align to alignment. SkinParam.setParam then processes these canonical keys in source order through a LinkedHashMap: an alias-equivalent reassignment changes the existing entry's value without moving its first insertion position, while style conversion observes the new value immediately. Thus stateArrowColor and ArrowColor are one arrowColor identity, no matter how often or with what case they alternate, and the last declaration sets root.element.stateDiagram.arrow LineColor. RustUML also has a separate compatibility representation for themes: its preprocessor appends a `__theme` marker and then flattens all theme family sub-blocks into scoped synthetic keys consumed by individual renderers. Those post-marker records must retain their family prefixes and raw-key replacement identity; treating them as ordinary Java declarations collapses distinct style scopes that Java selects before applying. GraphvizImageBuilder and SvekEdge independently merge the selected arrow signature and derive the shaft and arrowhead Rainbow from it. The arrow signature may inherit the root or theme line color, but never the state sibling's explicit LineColor. A per-link color remains the final arrow-only override.
causal_divergence: Commit 8289f2e0 correctly performs one renderer lookup across the two arrow aliases, but parse::collapse_reassigned_skinparams compares raw keys case-insensitively rather than comparing Java's cleanForKey identities. In an alternating sequence stateArrowColor, ArrowColor, stateArrowColor, ArrowColor, stateArrowColor, Rust collapses each raw spelling into a separate first-position slot and updates only its value. The final state-prefixed value remains in the earlier slot, so the renderer's reverse scan incorrectly selects the later-position global slot. Java canonicalizes all five declarations to arrowColor before replacement, leaving one entry with the final value. The rejected alternating-alias heldout isolates this as eight color-only shaft and arrowhead differences.
planned_change: Model SkinParam.cleanForKeySlow's ordinary-key identity in the parser's reassignment collapse: trim and lowercase, remove underscore and dot separators, normalize sequence aliases, normalize every family-arrow prefix to arrow, and normalize a terminal align to alignment. Before the synthetic theme-tail boundary, compare declarations by that canonical identity and apply LinkedHashMap-style first-position/last-value replacement while retaining the first stored spelling for compatibility with existing renderer lookups. Once `__theme` begins the appended compatibility tail, preserve the established case-insensitive raw-key replacement identity so distinct family scopes remain distinct; keep all double-underscore metadata as ordered events. Add a parser test proving user aliases canonicalize before a theme marker while synthetic family-arrow keys remain separate after it. Keep the renderer's one reverse source-order lookup, stateBorderColor isolation, root/theme fallback, and per-transition final override. Preserve every opposite-order, border-only, changed-count, theme, and local-link heldout. Do not special-case state fixtures, colors, counts, or geometry.
